But we can use ls with path? The ls tool only lists current directory. There's no tool to change directory. But we can use find with path? But we can't change cwd. Maybe we can use ls with path? The ls signature: ls({a?: boolean}). It doesn't accept path. So we cannot list arbitrary directories. But maybe we can use find to search from root? find has path param. So we can find all files under /tmp. But we want to list all files in /tmp. We can use find with path="/tmp" and name=None. That will return all items. But we also want hidden files. find will include hidden because it searches recursively. So we can call find with path="/tmp" and name="None"? Actually name param default "None" string. If None, all items returned. So we can call find({"path":"/tmp","name":"None"}). That will return list of items. Let's do that.
